2022 and 2024 boundaries are constructed from Thiessen polygons first run on each individual point, then grouped together by bureau to vote according to the home address to bureau de vote correspondence file published by INSEE. 2022 mappings are used for 2024; according to INSEE, “only 65 creations and 4 deletions of polling stations were observed between February 2023 and February 2024 (out of a total of 69,400 polling stations).” Note that this can produce enclaves which are nonetheless accurate. Thiessen polygons are only generated within, not across, municipalities; that is, the procedure is run one municipality at a time for all points assigned to the respective municipality. There are three exceptions: overseas departments of code 97, where I generate Thiessen from polling station addresses (type = “Thiessen”); units in Paris, which are reported exactly (type = “Actual”); and municipalities with only one polling station, which use the full municipality boundary (type = “Actual”).

Iranian election results are purportedly reported by city, though in some instances (Chardavol specifically) the unit is above or below that level; furthermore, there appears to be some degree of undercounting in the results. Polygons are obtained by getting “city” centroids then constructing Thiessen polygons, so between the apparent result undercounting and the absence of formal unit boundaries there is more error than expected on average here.
All votes reported are for first-preference.
House of Keys general elections in the 12 two-member constituencies of the 2013 boundaries, used unchanged in 2016, 2021 and 2026.

Each voter may cast up to two votes, so total_votes is the sum of candidate votes in the constituency and is roughly 1.7 to 1.9 times the number of voters. Votes are recorded by candidate; party is the ballot description on the Notice of Poll, and candidates without one are Independent.

The 2021 and 2026 figures are transcribed from hand-filled Notices of Result, read twice independently, and the two readings agree on every figure. No 2026 electorate by constituency was published, so reg and turnout_reg are missing for 2026.
Constituency polygons are the Isle of Man Government's House of Keys constituency boundaries.
Polling stations located in the West Bank are geocoded but lack Thiessen polygons.

notes: "Abroad" special type inferred using place names in NAME3, some of which are locations definitively outside Lebanon. The 2022 election publishes no polling-station coordinates, so 2022 stations are located by two routes recorded in geometry_type_b: reuse of a 2018 station coordinate where the station recurs, and fresh geocoding of the building name otherwise. Of 6,860 in-country units, 4,937 reuse a 2018 station and 556 are freshly geocoded to the building (80.1% station level); the remaining 1,367 fall back to a locality centroid (1,154 from 2018, 213 geocoded) because the source names the venue only generically, e.g. "the public school". Every in-country 2022 unit has a location; rows still marked Missing are out-of-country ("Abroad") voting, which has no location in Lebanon by construction.

sources: Commission électorale nationale indépendante pour la transition
notes: 2018 election aggregate vote counts differ from official reports, but candidate rank order and second round results are the same.
Malaysian coalition results align with Wikipedia aggregates, but there seem to be discrepancies in the vote-shares attained by the parties within each coalition.

Beginning with the 2013 election, results are provided at the saluran (polling-stream) level: each polling district (daerah mengundi) is divided into several streams that share one polling centre and the same geometry. The party column gives the ballot-symbol party (the coalition for BN/PH/PN/GPS or a standalone party), with the component party in party_b and the coalition in party_c. The 2008 election remains at parliamentary-constituency level. Polling-district polygons are Thiessen cells built from the district points (Tindak Malaysia daerah-mengundi centroids where available, otherwise Google-geocoded polling centres), because gazetted polling-district boundaries are not public for Sarawak and do not tile the country's unpopulated interior.
Votes are first-count (first-preference) votes under the Single Transferable Vote, summed from candidates to parties. Later-count transfers are not recorded.
The 13 electoral divisions are the finest published grain. Ballot boxes are mixed within each division before counting, so no locality or polling-station results exist.
Geometry is Missing for all years. Division boundaries are redrawn before each election and are published only as street-level descriptions, not as maps or polygons.

total_votes is the division's published valid vote, and turnout_reg is valid votes over the revised electoral register, so it runs a few points below the official turnout, which counts all ballots cast.
NAME3_imp is generated piece-wise: polling stations are spatially matched to municipality boundaries, then filled by NAME3 where NAME3 is not NA, then filled by NAME1, NAME2, and NAME4.

notes: Results are for the 92 local constituencies of the House of Representatives, with the same boundaries and seat counts in 2016, 2021 and 2026. The regional and national lists are reported only at region or national level and are not included.

Vote figures come from the Hespress election portal, which republishes the Ministry of the Interior's final results. The 2021 figures match the Ministry's own results file list for list, and the 2016 figures match Tafra's compilation. Hespress has no 2016 page for El Hajeb, so its 2016 lists come from Tafra.
total_votes is the sum of valid list votes in the constituency. Registered voters and invalid ballots are not published by constituency.

The 65 constituencies that are a whole province or prefecture use geoBoundaries ADM2 polygons. 23 split constituencies are unions of the OpenStreetMap communes and arrondissements named in Décret n° 2-11-603 (2011). Four split constituencies (Rabat-Océan, Rabat-Chellah, Marrakech-Ménara and Marrakech-Guéliz-Ennakhil) have Missing geometry because the decree divides them by units with no published boundaries.

Constituencies in Western Sahara are included. Laâyoune, Boujdour, Es-Semara, Oued Ed-Dahab and Aousserd lie wholly or almost wholly in the territory, and Tarfaya and Assa-Zag straddle its northern limit.
Lower house refers to the Pyithu Hluttaw despite no formal delineation.

sources: Secretaria-Geral do Ministério da Administração Interna
notes: Parish boundaries from 2001 are used for pre-2001 years.

Systematic missingness of polling station coordinates by region means that Thiessen polygons are generated separately by region by year. This is also necessary to address Russian annexation of Crimea and Sevastopol.

Tens of polling stations reported as belonging to Moscow Oblast in 2012 actually fall within the bounds of the Moscow federal subject; the region was manually adjusted to account for this discrepancy.

Results are reported at the polling-box level (boxes A1(a), A1(b), etc.) within each constituency. Polling boxes are not individually geolocated, so each box is assigned its constituency's polygon and centroid and is therefore flagged as a geocode duplicate.

Constituency polygons are constructed from OCHA cod-ab settlement boundaries: each settlement is assigned to a constituency by matching its name to voter addresses in the electoral register and taking the majority registered constituency, unmatched settlements are filled by the nearest matched settlement within the same quarter, and settlements are then unioned per constituency. The split-quarter seats (the five Castries constituencies and the Gros Islet/Babonneau, Vieux Fort, Micoud, and Dennery pairs) carry some boundary-reconstruction uncertainty because their settlement-to-seat assignment is inferred from voter registrations rather than an official schedule.
Election data are incomplete; Thiessen polygons generated within department boundaries for completed reports.
